text.p: Film Greats Turn out for Garden

Some venerable Hollywood names turned out today to dedicate a New York garden to Katharine Hepburn on her 90th birthday. Planners of the event say "Miss H," as director Anthony Harvey called her, remained at home in Fenwick, Conn. Harvey, who directed Hepburn in her Oscar-winning role in "The Lion in Winter," says she was doing well when he spoke to her over the weekend. The Katharine Hepburn Garden is part of Dag Hammarskjold Plaza at the United Nations. Other Hollywood greats on hand for the occasion included director and writer Garson Kanin, who wrote such Hepburn films as "Adam's Rib" and "Pat and Mike," and actor Sam Waterston.
Spector To Be Honoured

Phil Spector is expected to turn up in Beverly Hills tomorrow to share an award for the 1960s pop classic, "You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin'." The song, which Spector co-wrote with Barry Mann and Cynthia Weil, will be honoured for having logged seven million plays on the radio, according to Broadcast Music Inc. The award will be presented at BMI's annual Pop Awards, honouring the most performed songs in the BMI repertoire for the past year. "You've Lost That Lovin' Feeling'," a No. 1 hit for the Righteous Brothers in 1965, stands as BMI's most performed song, surpassing the six million tally of the Beatles' "Yesterday."
Cannes Lackluster

Halfway into the Cannes film festival today, no clear favourite has emerged for the Golden Palm award in a largely uninspiring competition. In an attempt to escape a competition diet heavy on dark, violent tales, filmgoers hoped Stephan Elliott's "Welcome to Woop Woop" would provide some Australian light relief at a midnight screening. Critics' polls give "Welcome To Sarajevo" by Britain's Michael Winterbottom, the tale of a journalist's adoption of a Bosnian girl, and "Western," an oddball road movie by Manuel Poirier, a narrow lead in the Golden Palm contest.
Johnny Depp, 'Quiet American'

Besides premiering his directorial debut film "The Brave," Johnny Depp is eyeing future work while at the Cannes Film Festival. Depp is meeting former jury president Sydney Pollack in Cannes to discuss a planned $40 million production of Graham Greene's "The Quiet American." Industry sources say Depp may star in the espionage story alongside Sean Connery, who has already signed up for the movie to be directed by "The Saint" helmer Phillip Noyce.
Variety, Miramax Launch Tome

Variety editor-in-chief Peter Bart and Miramax Films co-chairman Harvey Weinstein hosted a party to celebrate the publication of Miramax Books' "Fifty Years of Sun, Sex & Celluloid," a history of the Cannes Film Festival by the editors of Variety. Among those attending were Jack Palance, "Copland" co-star Annabella Sciorra, "The English Patient" producer Saul Zaentz, Brad Krevoy and Steve Stabler of Motion Picture Corp. of America and film critic Roger Ebert.
Cannes Kids Get Star Treatment

Nobody said it's easy being a working mother, but when the work involves presiding over the jury at the Cannes Film Festival, as is the case for French actress Isabelle Adjani, having a young family is particularly tough. Adjani has manoeuvred around part of the problem, though. She persuaded festival organisers to open a day-care centre for the stars -- or rather for the stars' offspring. Adjani's two children are bound for Les Kids du Festival facility.
WB Adding Dramas

The WB Network will reveal this week that Tuesday will be its new fourth night of primetime programming, featuring two new dramas to distinguish itself from the comedies and movies on other webs that night. Monday and Wednesday nights will stay mainly the same on the netlet, while Sunday nights will showcase two new comedies, one with Tom Arnold and another starring comedian Carol Leifer. WB will announce its lineup tomorrow.
Minghella to Direct 'Cigarettes'

Oscar-winning director Anthony Minghella has signed to direct a feature version of his radio play "Cigarettes and Chocolate" for Miramax Films. The piece, originally written and performed for BBC Radio in 1988, is about a woman who opts to give up speaking, causing her family and friends to blame themselves and make extraordinary confessions to her. The project is to be one of Minghella's next three pictures. There is no word on the other two.
Threat to Quit UK Ungrounded

Andrew Lloyd Webber, the world's best-paid composer, had threatened to emigrate if the Labour party was elected to run Britain. With little love lost between Lloyd Webber and many ordinary Britons, a vote for Labour was duly billed as a 2-for-1 deal by vote-hunting politicians. Labour lived up to its side of the bargain by clinching a landslide victory in the May 1 election. But Lloyd Webber is still there. Aides now say Lloyd Webber would only consider leaving the country if Labour brought in punitive new taxes.
TNT Plans Eastwood Documentary

TNT plans to make Clint Eastwood's day by producing a documentary featuring rare footage and exclusive interviews with the actor/director. Sources say Time magazine critic Richard Schickel will write, produce and direct the documentary, getting the same access from Eastwood that he got for his best-selling "Clint Eastwood: A Biography." Eastwood will also let TNT's cameras film him on the set of "Midnight in the Garden of Good & Evil," the movie he's directing for Warner Bros. The documentary will run on TNT sometime in the fall.
